 Ananya Panday calls all 3 exes—Aditya Roy Kapur, Ishaan Khatter, Kartik Aaryan—on KWK
 Ananya Panday spoke about being single and wanting to fall in love with herself, while Ananya Birla opened up about her complicated love life and privilege.
 Tarini Unnikrishnan

 New Delhi: Ananya Panday has come a long way from being coy. On this week’s episode of Koffee with Karan, the actor was rather open about her past relationships, calling three of her exes—Aditya Roy Kapur, Ishaan Khatter and Kartik Aaryan—during a game. All three picked up.
 Panday accompanied entrepreneur Ananya Birla, a fifth-generation member of the Birla business family, on Wednesday’s episode of Koffee with Karan Season 9. The two spoke about relationships, privilege and careers. Shanaya Kapoor later joined them as a surprise third contestant for the Rapid Fire.
 Johar began by teasing Panday about her relationships. According to him, she could be heartbroken on a Friday and perfectly fine by Monday. Panday didn’t entirely disagree.
 Show Full Article
 “It is true that I have been in a few relationships, but I honestly don’t think that there’s anything wrong with that,” she said. “I feel I was born to get married. I love the idea of getting married. I’m excited to be with one person for my entire life. And I feel like if something’s not working, if people are not happy, if you’re not a hundred percent sure, then you’re very well within your right to get out of something and move.”
 For now, she’s enjoying being single. Panday admitted she had spent too much time prioritising relationships and wanted to fall back in love with herself before dating again.
 Birla’s love life, on the other hand, is complicated. She described herself as a hopeless romantic who often falls for the wrong people. She also revealed that she’d received repeated marriage proposals from someone from another wealthy business family, but wouldn’t name him.
 Love lives to nepotism 
 The conversation soon veered to that familiar Koffee with Karan subject—nepotism. Birla didn’t deny her privilege.
 “I probably have had things easier, but you don’t choose where you’re born. All you can do is make the most of that situation,” she said.
 She also spoke about sexism in boardrooms, where men sometimes treat her as “daddy’s little girl”, but said that in business, numbers eventually speak for themselves.
 Panday, meanwhile, revisited her infamous remarks about struggling in Bollywood.
 “It’s a trigger word because I made a very stupid statement nine years ago or eight years ago. Obviously, people haven’t forgotten,” she said.
 During Koffee Shots, a version of Truth or Drink, Johar asked whether either had ever had an entire venue cleared for a date.
 “Are people doing this?” Panday asked.
 Birla took a shot.
 “She’s quite a romantic,” Panday said.
 “And rich!” Johar added.
 Then came Hey Karan, It’s Me, which has a new twist this season. Guests must call a celebrity friend and confuse them before revealing they’re on the show.
 Panday called Roy Kapur, who was in hospital with dengue. She kept asking whether he had heard what had happened, leaving him confused before finally explaining the real reason she was calling.
 Next she called Khatter. She began apologising, saying she’d done something terrible. But he caught on, almost immediately asking why she was performing so badly.
 For her turn, Birla called Tamannaah Bhatia and Alia Bhatt, telling both that something had happened and she didn’t know what to do. Both Bhatt and Bhatia seemed worried, till Birla revealed the joke.
 Panday wanted to make one more call, this time on video. Johar agreed, provided the person was famous enough.
 “He’s big only,” Panday assured him.
 It was Kartik Aaryan. He answered, and Johar got him to say the required line. Panday argued she deserved ten points for making a video call.
 “You’ve called all of your exes,” Birla pointed out. Panday didn’t deny it. “Record breaker,” she said, before worrying that her mother wouldn’t let her back into the house.

 The surprise entry 
 Johar then surprised Panday by bringing out childhood friend Shanaya Kapoor, who recently appeared in Student of the Year: After Dark (2026). Panday burst into tears, and the two hugged.
 During the Rapid Fire, Kapoor was asked what she and Panday both wanted.
 “Ranveer Singh,” she replied. And who should Panday date next? “No one. No one. No one,” came her pat-reply.
 Asked about the rudest but funniest thing she’d read about herself online, Kapoor’s answer made Johar wince.
 “That I beat my dad to the longest delayed debut,” she said, referring to her father Sanjay Kapoor.
 Panday admitted to being insecure about almost everything, including her appearance, speech and dancing. She chose Jungle Mein Mangal (1972) as the film title for her last relationship, prompting Johar to ask if the Jungle referred to Vantara.
 Birla recalled being told, “For a girl, you’re really good,” when asked about patronising remarks she’d heard as a businesswoman. She also chose Shah Rukh Khan to play her father in a biopic.
 (Edited by Janaki Pande)
